RESEARCH RELEASE 1.0 · HF1–HF4-B5

How the common horizon changes

Surfaces from numerical simulations, curvature maps and selected regions — with checks of what these images actually show.

The project reconstructs and compares available data from three separate configurations. Colour represents calculated quantities and surface regions selected by an explicit criterion.

01 / RECONSTRUCTIONS

Three sources. Three different questions.

HF1 / HF1R · SXS:BBH:0305 · Lev6

A selected region on the surface

Actual coordinates of common apparent horizon C. R*, E* and B* map intrinsic surface curvature and the normal components of the electric and magnetic parts of the Weyl tensor.

The bright region is a component satisfying the preserved angular-gradient criterion. This is an operational definition of a “latent structure”, not an established independent object.

1.566 snapshots and 4.698 mask correspondences checked. The interactive viewer contains 235 selected frames. Late snapshots are shown separately, without invented transitions.

Rotate the surface and change the field

HF3 / HF4-B2–B5 · EINSTEIN TOOLKIT · QC0

From two horizons to a common horizon

Saved individual surfaces from 0 to 22M and 55 common-horizon frames starting at 18.625M. Re Ψ₂, Im Ψ₂ and the shear magnitude |σ| are available on the common horizon.

Masks mark approximately 5% of physical area with the strongest field deviation from the median. Area was reconstructed from the tetrad and checked against diagnostics from the same run.

Individual horizons are missing at four times. Gaps are identified in the viewer. QC0 evolution and wave time series reach 105M; this viewer’s geometry reaches 22M.

Open the QC0 horizons

YITIAN / HF4-A1–A2 · SXS:BBH:0389 · SpEC

Geometry through multipoles

Mass and spin moments through ℓ=8 allow scalar angular maps to be reconstructed. The atlas shows the full field, its deviation from the late state and the effect of rotating coordinates.

Here, a spherical map represents a field. A finite set of moments does not determine a unique complete shape of the early horizon.

301 atlas frames from 0 to 150M. Time zero is the first appearance of the common horizon in this simulation.

Open the dynamic atlas

02 / FINAL STAGE

What the angular expansion explains

HF4-B5 uses the saved QC0 fields and B4 physical-area weights. Expansions through ℓ=2, 4, 6 and 8 were checked on all 55 frames. Previous calculations were not rerun.

Fraction of angular variation described by components through ℓ=8
FieldRange over timeAt t=22M
Re Ψ₂96.388–99.977%99.97664%
Im Ψ₂99.074–99.962%99.96240%
|σ|99.815–99.936%99.81524%

This is weighted variation on the same nodes used for fitting. These percentages are not simulation accuracy, physical energy or probabilities that the model is correct.

The main pattern is compact. The residual needs careful interpretation.

In the first Re Ψ₂ frame, two nodes account for 83.14% of the squared residual norm at ℓ≤8. They occupy approximately 0.281% of the discrete area measure. The nodes are retained; these data do not establish their origin.

This result constrains the interpretation of the local feature. A claim of an independent physical phenomenon requires resolution, coordinate and tetrad checks.

03 / SCIENTIFIC RESULTS

What the available data establish

QC0 ringdown

The final HF3 check reaches 105M. In the third period at radii 15, 30 and 40M, the free complex fit differs from the Kerr reference by 0.0034–0.1072% in frequency and 0.72–1.51% in damping.

This is descriptive agreement. Statistical acceptance of the Kerr model under a calibrated error model is not claimed.

Method and corrected reference

Reconstructed QC0 geometry

The physical area of 55 common surfaces agrees with QLM from the same run: the maximum relative difference is 6.04 × 10⁻⁸. The saved fields have different longitudinal and polar localisation.

This checks processing consistency, not the physical error of the simulation.

Area, measures and localisation

04 / RELEASE SCOPE

A completed project with explicit limits

Release 1.0 completes reconstruction and descriptive validation of the available dataset. Unresolved questions are retained as research outcomes.

Included

  • Actual coordinate surfaces for HF1 and QC0.
  • Scalar maps and evolution from Yitian’s multipoles.
  • Videos, interactive viewers, tables and programs.
  • Ringdown, area, angular-component and residual checks.

Not yet established

  • Continuous validated QC0 geometry from 0 to 105M.
  • Resolution convergence of local residuals and independence from coordinates and tetrad.
  • Physical identity of the HF1 and QC0 regions, or evidence of new physics.
  • Complete modelling of Yitian’s early dynamics and unique identification of nonlinear components.

The project shows apparent horizons and explicitly labelled scalar maps. It does not reconstruct the global event horizon or produce a ray-traced optical image.

Materials you can inspect

Stage reports, tables, programs, data provenance and the exact checkpoint for continuation.
